preamble: Final *-r became the velar stop *-k in Proto-Northern Chin (Kuki-Chin, Tibeto-Burman), one of the innovations VanBik (2009) uses to define the Northern (Zo) subgroup. Central Chin languages such as Hakha Lai and Mizo keep the rhotic coda (pâar 'flower', thar 'new'), while Northern Chin Tedim and Paite show -k; Thado Kuki then shifted this -k further to a glottal stop.

examples.note: Hakha Lai thâr; Thado Kuki thâʔ shows the later -k > -ʔ step.

examples.from: Proto-Kuki-Chin *baar 'eat with the palm of the hand'

sources: VanBik, K. (2009). Proto-Kuki-Chin: A Reconstructed Ancestor of the Kuki-Chin Languages. STEDT Monograph 8. https://stedt.johnblowe.com/pubs_and_prods/STEDT_Monograph8_Proto-Kuki-Chin.pdf
